recipes.name: Beef au Jus
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt drippings in a skillet over medium-high heat. Whisk in flour and cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens, about 3 minutes.
Add beef broth gradually, whisking constantly, then increase heat to high and bring to a boil.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Beef au Jus
raw_recipe.description: This easy au jus recipe from Chef John combines beef drippings with broth to make a rich and flavorsome au jus perfect for prime rib or for dipping.

video.description: Get ready for a mouthwatering experience with this delicious Beef Au Jus recipe. In this video, Chef John reveals the most minimalist method for creating a quick and flavorful au jus to complement your prime rib of beef. With rich, meaty flavors and a simple ingredient list, this au jus is the perfect accompaniment to your next prime rib roast or French dip sandwich. Chef John shares step-by-step instructions, including tips for achieving the perfect consistency and storing leftovers. Whether you're a seasoned cook or a beginner in the kitchen, this recipe will elevate your beef dishes to new heights of flavor and satisfaction.

review.reviewBody: Very easy. I didn't have beef drippings, so used margarine, and used water and Better than Bullion for the beef broth. Takes 5 minutes, and was good with the Beef and Roasted Red Pepper Sandwiches I made it for. I ended up with more than I needed, so I just tossed the remainder in a soup I'm putting together for the crock pot. If you added more flour, this would also make some beef gravy. Thanks for the recipe!

If I could give this more than 5 stars, I would. I used some leftover eye of round roast, sliced it really thin (for French dips), and simmered it in beef broth, a splash of Worcestershire, and about 1/2 tsp of fajita seasoning. When the meat was tender, I used that broth for my 2 cups of broth. I hadn’t saved any drippings. Following some of the other reviews, I used butter. I did let the butter brown just a bit before I added the flour. This is incredible!!! It will be my go-to in the future. I’m saving the extra for a vegi-beef soup. Highly recommend!

I had to double the flour as there was way too much fat, once I did that, this looked great. It was a bit bland though, and something was missing. It didn't have much depth of flavor and I feel like this would benefit from some worcestershire and maybe onion powder too. I did add quite a lot of freshly ground black pepper but it was still lacking something. I used Better Than Bouillion roasted beef flavor and water to make a beef broth. Overall, this was okay. If you use a highly seasoned meat and render more flavorful drippings, you'll get a better Au Jus. I let this cook a little longer so it would thicken a bit more and put it over an open faced beef sandwich and potatoes. This would be great if you had leftover beef that needs a sauce or gravy to add moisture, which is what I used it for.

My husband, who is the chef in this household, could not stop complementing me on this jus. I’ve never made something like this, but it’s super easy to do. I used prime rib scraps for “drippings”, frying them in a cast iron skillet since we were smoking the prime rib on the Traeger, then added some beef concentrate for a little stronger flavor. Delicious!

I've made Chef John's prime rib for years, and it's always perfect. However, the au jus consistently fails. The high initial heat burns the drippings, ruining the flavor. I've tried adding stock to the pan to prevent burning, but it doesn't help. I've resorted to making the au jus without the drippings, which I know is a crime, but it ensures a good meal. Any suggestions?

I didn't have beef drippings, just a deli package of thin sliced uncooked beef but I used beef broth and a seasoned flour mixture and simmered it, then I stuffed the beef in hot dog buns that I needed to use, covered with swiss for him and Colby + Monterrey jack cheeses for me and zapped them in the micro for a minute. Put them in a large shallow bowl for each with a potato with garlic butter on it and then spooned the lovely Au Ju over the potatoes and dipped our cut sandwiches in it - favorite new dish!! I almost never eat this many carbs in one meal but we worked all day with no lunch so we deserved the treat!

i used beef lard rather then drippings which in retrospect was probably a little heavy handed. probably would cut the beef lard down to match the flour next time, 1.5 T. I also used bone broth that i made from beef marrow bones and the texture was silky and intoxicating. and i supplemented the beef flavor that my bone broth was lacking with beef base and the finished product was really perfect. so good.

Perfect, even after I had to modify. I was out of beef broth so used 1 cup of chicken broth and 1 cup Merlot. The Fond, juices and fat were enough to give it a very beefy flavor. Everyone loved it. After the beef was gone I used the leftovers to make a gravy by mixing with a bit more roux. I use this method for all my gravies now. Super simple, super tasty.

I added red wine to bottom of pan while roasting the meat. 
Have a great taste!
Use less flour. Start with a little and work your way up. Mine ended up gravy-like because I just dumped it in.

This was the hit of our Prime Rib dinner. Instead of 1/4 cup of drippings I used 1 cup of drippings and reduced the amount of beef broth required. Glad I have left over. It goes great on left over mashed potatoes,
Perfect for any prime rib you would make
Not great, not horrible, just OK. What it's missing is some nice dry red wine.
I added a splash of worsh sauce and soy sauce. And garlic. Very tasty an jus!
This took more beef broth than the recipe stated to get the right texture that he shows in the video, but it was really great. Made it with his prime rib recipe, which was also great!
Thank you Chef John! Today I used your Prime Rib Roast calculation, your au jus recipe, and your Horseradish Sauce recipe for Christmas dinner. Everything was a hit!
